questions.question: What is the typical format of the written English exam?
options: Part 1 with short-answer tasks and Part 2 with a long text, over 5 hours
questions.explanation: The written exam typically has short-answer tasks (e.g. comparing sources) and a long text, within 5 hours.

questions.question: Which resources are allowed during the written exam?
options: Digital resources, but not AI tools
questions.explanation: Digital resources are allowed, but AI tools and communication with others are not.

questions.question: What should you identify before writing your long text?
options: The text type, required content and expected structure
The number of paragraphs other students write
questions.explanation: Task analysis — identifying text type, content and structure requirements — prevents answering the wrong question.

questions.question: What writing tip does the chapter give about the introduction?
options: Make the introduction half the essay
Copy the introduction from the source material
questions.explanation: Outlining first and possibly writing the introduction last helps it match what you actually wrote.

questions.question: Which are common pitfalls on the written exam?
options: Not answering the question, running out of time, poor paragraphing and not proofreading
questions.explanation: The classic pitfalls are missing the question, poor time management, weak paragraphing and skipping proofreading.
